learningObjective: Distinguish dead code elimination from unreachable code elimination and identify soundness conditions.

canonicalClaims.claim: DCE removes instructions that (1) produce a value with no live uses and (2) have no observable side effects. Unreachable code elimination is a distinct pass that removes CFG blocks not reachable from entry.
conditions: IR distinguishes pure from side-effecting operations.
Language/target semantics define what counts as an observable side effect (I/O, memory writes, exceptions, volatile access).
nonImplications: Does not imply all loads can be removed; volatile and side-effecting loads must remain.
Does not imply a single DCE pass captures all dead code; iteration with other optimizations often uncovers more.

misconceptions.claim: Any pure computation with unused result can be removed by DCE regardless of possible exceptions.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Floating-point exceptions or divide-by-zero traps are observable side effects in strict-FP or trap-on-signal environments; removing them can change program behavior.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: EAC3 DCE chapter; LLVM strict FP semantics

misconceptions.whyWrong: DCE can be implemented on non-SSA IRs using reaching-definition and liveness analysis; SSA simplifies but is not required.

misconceptions.claim: Unreachable code elimination is a special case of DCE.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Unreachable code elimination is CFG-based (control flow); DCE is data-flow-based (unused values). They compose but are distinct.

implementationFacts: LLVM has separate passes: DeadCodeElimination, AggressiveDCE (ADCE), and UnreachableBlockElim.
ADCE assumes all code is dead until proven live by walking backward from side-effecting instructions and terminators.
performanceScenarios: Iterating SCCP + DCE + simplification is a canonical mid-end optimization pattern.
